Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

scopusflow (development version)

New features

  • scopus_fetch_plan() gains cursor, so a plan cell matching more than 5000 records can be retrieved whole and still be checkpointed. The default, cursor = FALSE, keeps the offset paging plans have always used. Checkpoints now record the paging mode and serve only a request in the same mode, and one written before the mode was recorded counts as offset-paged. A checkpoint in the other mode is refetched with a warning that names both modes. Inside a plan, the warning for a cell that stops at the offset ceiling now names scopus_fetch_plan(plan, cursor = TRUE). It used to advise partitioning by year, which a year-partitioned plan already does. The search record’s reproduction snippet passes cursor = TRUE when the records were paged by cursor. The Python twin’s fetch_plan() gains cursor too, and keeps the cursor paging it has always used unless given cursor=False.
  • scopus_fetch(), scopus_fetch_plan() and scopus_records() gain fields = "extended", adding the document type, source type, volume, issue, pages, ISSN, PubMed identifier and open-access status the Search API already returns, and the abstract under the COMPLETE view, at no extra quota. summary() reports how many records ‘Scopus’ labels errata or retracted, and the help pages explain why those labels do not screen a set for retractions. Checkpoints record their fields. An extended checkpoint serves a core request with the extra columns dropped. A core checkpoint is a miss for an extended request and is refetched with a warning. read_scopus_records() keeps the extended columns of a .csv file, as text apart from the integer open_access, so an ISSN keeps its leading zeros. The default, fields = "core", returns the columns it always has. The Python twin’s fetch_plan() and to_records() gain fields too.
  • With fields = "extended", as_ris() and as_bibtex() type conference papers, conference reviews, chapters and books by the document type ‘Scopus’ gives them (RIS CPAPER, CONF, CHAP and BOOK, BibTeX @inproceedings, @incollection and @book), where every record used to be a journal article. The entries carry the volume, issue, pages, ISSN and document type, and under view = "COMPLETE" the abstract, which screening and de-duplication tools read. A COMPLETE set also exports its author keywords, one RIS KW line each, with or without the extended fields. A value the record lacks is left out. The Python twin’s to_ris() and to_bibtex() do the same, held to a shared golden file.
  • scopus_abstract(include = "index_terms") returns the index keywords ‘Scopus’ assigns, in an idxterms column joined by "; ", under view = "FULL". scopus_corpus() can use them, alone or with the author keywords, through its new keywords argument, "index" or "both", and refuses either under view = "REF" before any request. The default, keywords = "author", keeps the author keywords alone. ‘Scopus’ chooses index keywords from standard vocabularies, so they give different co-occurrence results from author keywords, and whether they arrive depends on the key’s entitlement. In development testing, they arrived on a key whose author keywords came back empty. The Python twin’s scopus_abstract() and corpus() gain the same options.
  • write_scopus_corpus() writes a scopus_corpus() result in theoryforge’s corpus schema, keying cited works on the ‘Scopus’ identifier so the same work is one node however its DOI is written. as_theoryforge_corpus() returns the same document as a list. A reference that carries only a DOI takes the identifier that another document or reference in the corpus pairs with that DOI, and one with neither is dropped with a warning. Keywords are trimmed, lower-cased and made unique, and a missing year is written as null. Keyed on the DOI wherever there was one, as theoryforge’s own recipe did, two documents citing the same two works gave no co-citation edge. A provenance block records the search expression, when the search ran, the kind of keyword and how many references were dropped and records came without keywords. The Python twin’s write_corpus() and to_theoryforge_corpus() write the same bytes, held to a shared golden file and validated against a copy of theoryforge’s schema.
  • scopus_diff_records() compares two harvests record by record, matching on the ‘Scopus’ identifier and, where a record lacks one, on the DOI, as scopus_combine(dedupe = TRUE) matches records. Each row gives the record’s citation counts in both harvests beside its status, identifier, DOI, title and year. A record in one harvest only whose DOI the other harvest gives to a different record is marked conflict for you to check, since it may have been re-indexed under a new identifier or may be a distinct paper sharing the DOI. Records with neither key are counted and left out. The Python twin’s diff_records() returns the same rows, held to a shared fixture.

Changed behaviour

  • scopus_corpus() now reports the requests it made and the quota left, in the n_requests and quota attributes, as the Python twin does, and both twins return each document’s ‘Scopus’ identifier in a new scopus_id column, the second. It comes from Abstract Retrieval, or from the records where the lookup failed. Code that selects the corpus’s columns by position needs updating. The result also carries the search expression, when the search ran and the kind of keyword, as the attributes query, retrieved_at and keywords, which write_scopus_corpus() records.

  • Input errors now inherit scopus_error, as the package has always documented. scopus_error_bad_input was raised on its own, so tryCatch(scopus_error = ...) let a blank query or an out-of-range year through. Invalid view, partition, by, .op and style values now raise scopus_error_bad_input too, where they were bare rlang_error conditions with the same message. A retry loop keyed on scopus_error should test the subclass, since an input error will not succeed on retry.

  • scopus_abstract() now requests view = "META_ABS" by default, the view Elsevier documents as carrying the abstract, as the Python twin does. It used to send no view and so took the API’s default, which Elsevier documents as META, a view without the abstract. A live request in October 2026 nonetheless returned the abstract without a view, so earlier default calls may well have carried it. The column no longer depends on behaviour the documentation contradicts. Pass view = NULL to send the old request. A default call’s checkpoints are now keyed META_ABS. A cache written by 0.4.0 for a call without a view therefore serves only view = NULL, and a default call spends a request on each of its identifiers again.

  • Queries are checked offline before any request. LIMIT-TO() and EXCLUDE() refinement syntax pasted from the web interface, a field tag wrapped around a query that already opens with one, and unbalanced brackets, quotation marks or braces now raise scopus_error_bad_input in scopus_plan(), scopus_count(), scopus_fetch(), scopus_trend(), scopus_compare_topics() and scopus_intersections(). The Search API ignores a refinement without an error, so such a search ran unfiltered. A nested field tag failed with HTTP 400 after spending a request, and unbalanced brackets reached the API unchecked. INDEXTERMS(), which pybliometrics documents as not working through the Search API, raises a scopus_warning_query_syntax warning. The messages match the Python twin’s word for word. Given .field, scopus_query() now refuses a term that already opens with a field tag, where scopus_query("TITLE(x)", .field = "ABS") used to give ABS(TITLE(x)). scopus_intersections() uses a concept written as the web interface writes a tag, TITLE-ABS-KEY ( x ), as given, where it used to wrap it in field a second time.

  • RIS records put the source title under T2, which reference managers read as the publication title, instead of JO, which Zotero reads as the journal abbreviation, and now carry DB - Scopus and the EID as AN.

  • as_bibliometrix() follows the conventions bibliometrix::convert2df() applies to a ‘Scopus’ export, so its frame describes a record as a ‘Scopus’ CSV import does. AU gives each author as the surname and initials without full stops ("ZHANG F", where it held "ZHANG F."), joined by ";", and a COMPLETE name such as "Tour, James M." becomes "TOUR JM". UT holds the upper-cased EID, "2-S2.0-<scopus_id>", where it held the bare identifier, which sub("^2-S2.0-", "", UT) restores. A set carrying author keywords gains DE, and one retrieved with fields = "extended" gains DT, VL and IS.

  • Requests are retried after transport failures such as timeouts and connection resets, which httr2 stopped doing by default in 1.0.4, so one such failure no longer aborts a harvest. scopusflow now requires httr2 1.0.4 or later. A timeout is reported as such, with the class scopus_error_timeout (a subclass of scopus_error_offline), and no longer as being offline.

  • De-duplication in scopus_combine() now cleans DOIs as scopus_extract_dois() does (resolver prefixes, case) and matches a record without a ‘Scopus’ identifier to the identified record carrying the same DOI. Records with different identifiers and one DOI are still both kept, since ‘Scopus’ also gives one DOI to distinct papers, and the merge now counts them for you to check. The combined attribute records the rule as rule and the DOIs such records share as doi_conflicts, and PRISMA-S item 16 of the search record names the rule and gives the count. dedupe = "id_or_doi" merges records with different identifiers that share a DOI, and dedupe = "id_then_doi" reproduces the earlier rule. A set merged by 0.4.0 records no rule and keeps its item 16 wording. A blank identifier, which read_scopus_records() reads from a CSV file the Python twin wrote, now counts as none, where every record carrying one was merged into one record. dedupe refuses a value other than TRUE, FALSE or the name of a rule, where NA or any other value meant no de-duplication.

  • A logical argument that is not TRUE or FALSE now raises scopus_error_bad_input before any request: cursor and verbose in scopus_fetch(), resume and verbose in scopus_fetch_plan(), scopus_abstract() and scopus_corpus(), verbose in scopus_trend(), scopus_compare_topics() and scopus_intersections(), dedupe in scopus_extract_dois() and create in scopus_cache_dir(). isTRUE() read "TRUE", 1 and NA alike as FALSE, so scopus_fetch(cursor = "TRUE") paged by offset under the ceiling the caller meant to lift, and any other value died on a base error that a handler for scopus_error could not catch.

  • An empty years vector places no year restriction, as NULL does and as the Python twin reads an empty list. scopus_plan(), scopus_count() and scopus_fetch() died on an untyped formatting error building a date range from it, and scopus_trend() and scopus_compare_topics(), which count each year, now refuse it with the typed error a missing years already raised.

Bug fixes

  • The app’s search record no longer gives the bundled corpus’s own phrase as the search expression of a demo harvest, in a methods paragraph written to be pasted into a manuscript. In demo mode the record now names no expression, and it opens by saying that the records were replayed and that it describes no search that was run. Where the records came from is fixed when the harvest starts, so switching Demo mode afterwards does not change the record. The Python app does the same.
  • The app’s Check size button no longer closes the session on a blank query. The handler caught scopus_error alone, so the input error escaped it and Shiny ended the session. Check size and Fetch now refuse a blank query with a notification, as Compare and the Python app already did, and any other failure in Check size is shown as a notification.
  • scopus_compare_topics() joined the reference and each comparison term without brackets, so a reference containing OR or AND NOT was regrouped by the operator precedence of ‘Scopus’. Under the documented order, which applies AND NOT last, an AND NOT reference took the term into its negation, so the comparison set could exceed the reference and shares passed 100%. The join is now (reference) AND (term), as scopus_intersections() already wrote it. Re-run comparisons whose reference contains OR or AND NOT.
  • scopus_query() now brackets each term of several words when it joins two or more terms without a field tag, since ‘Scopus’ joins the words of an unquoted term with AND. scopus_query("machine learning", "deep learning", .op = "OR") used to give machine learning OR deep learning, which reads as machine AND (learning OR deep) AND learning. Quoted and braced phrases, bracketed groups and single field-tagged groups are left as written, and single words are never bracketed, so scopus_query("CRISPR", "Cas9", .op = "OR") is unchanged. Terms are also trimmed of the white space the Python twin trims, no-break spaces included.
  • A reference list that arrives as a single bare object, which is how Elsevier’s JSON sends a one-item array, no longer aborts the whole scopus_abstract() or scopus_corpus() batch, and every resume of it, with an untyped “subscript out of bounds” error. Neither does a cited work whose author list arrives that way. Any other shape the keyword or reference parser cannot read is now handled as a malformed response (scopus_error_malformed). That identifier gets a row of NAs and a warning and is retried on resume, while the rest of the batch completes. A lone author-keyword entry that carries no text, such as {"@_fa": "true"}, no longer becomes the keyword “true”.
  • The authors column held only the first author. The Search API’s dc:creator field is the first author alone, and the author list exists only under view = "COMPLETE", where scopusflow ignored it. Under COMPLETE the column now lists the authors as "Surname, Given", joined by "; " (up to the API’s 100 per record), so author tallies, as_bibliometrix() and the BibTeX and RIS exports see every author. Under STANDARD it still holds the first author, and scopus_top(by = "author") and as_bibliometrix() now say so once per session, as a note on the app’s Top authors tab does. Retrievals record their view as the view attribute, which a combined set keeps where its parts agree. COMPLETE-view checkpoints written by earlier versions are refetched once, and STANDARD ones are served as before. This corrects the 0.1.0 entry, which said the column retained every author a record lists.
  • Under view = "REF", scopus_abstract() returned only the first page of a reference list, about 40 references, which the documentation blamed on the API. It now follows startref until the list is complete, as pybliometrics does, at a cost of one request per 40 references, and n_requests counts each page. A REF reference’s title and source are now read, where both were always NA. REF cache files are keyed REF-paged, so truncated ones written by 0.4.0 are refetched once. This reaches scopus_corpus(view = "REF") too.
  • BibTeX and RIS exports wrote names in the ‘Scopus’ form “Surname I.”, with no comma, so BibTeX and biber took the initials for the family name and sorted bibliographies by them, and Zotero kept each RIS author as a single field. This touched every export of records retrieved outside COMPLETE. A name ending in initials is now written “Surname, I.”, and BibTeX titles protect words such as CRISPR-Cas9 and DNA from lower-casing. BibTeX also spaces run-together initials (“J. R.”), which it would otherwise read as one given name. The authors column and the citation keys are unchanged.
  • A spent weekly quota is no longer treated as a transient rate limit. Elsevier answers both with HTTP 429, and a response marked QUOTA_EXCEEDED now raises scopus_error_quota_exceeded (a subclass of scopus_error_rate_limit) naming the reset time, and is not retried. It stops a scopus_abstract() or scopus_corpus() batch with the rows already retrieved kept, an NA row for each identifier not retrieved and one scopus_warning_quota_exceeded warning. Every remaining identifier used to be tried three times and become an NA row with a warning of its own. The 403 message no longer blames the quota, and Retry-After dates parse in any locale, where a German or French LC_TIME made every one NA. scopus_quota() documents reset as the time the key’s quota resets, not a rate-limit window.
  • The search record dated a harvest by its earliest cell, although PRISMA-S item 13 asks for the date of the last search. Retrievals now carry retrieved_until beside retrieved_at. For the harvest of a plan, or a set from scopus_combine(), it holds the latest of its parts’ times, as retrieved_at holds the earliest. A search run over several sessions, or a baseline merged with its update, is now dated from its first retrieval to its last, item 13 gives the date of the last search, and the methods paragraph says the literature was searched between the two dates. Stamps on one UTC day give the single date they always gave.
  • A set without a plan no longer says “no year limit” when its limit is only unrecorded, and no longer lists item 8 of PRISMA-S as supplied. scopus_fetch() now attaches the one-cell plan it ran, so its record states the field tag and the years. A one-cell plan supplied for a set without per-cell counts keeps the set’s own counts, which the record used to call unrecorded. Year cells with gaps between them are listed, as in “2015, 2020 and 2025”, where the record gave one span that claimed the years between. Item 2, on databases searched together on one platform, is now supplied, since the API searches Scopus alone.
  • A harvest capped by max_results is now recorded as capped: the search record names the cap in the cells, the completeness line and item 9, the reproduction snippet passes it, and autoplot() says the bars count retrieved records. The app no longer caps live harvests at 200 records per year by default. Its field, now labelled “Max records per cell”, starts blank, and a note in the Retrieval panel says when the cap stopped a cell. scopus_fetch() and scopus_fetch_plan() keep a finite cap as the max_results attribute, which the record reads.
  • Closing one tab of the app deleted every other tab’s checkpoints mid-harvest, because the app kept its checkpoints by search alone and each session’s end removed the directory all sessions shared. Each session now keeps them in a temporary directory of its own, removed when that session ends, and a search fetched again in the same tab, after Cancel or a failure, resumes from them. The app article no longer promises that a quota-limited run picks up where it left off, which the temporary directory never allowed across sessions, and points to the generated script for a harvest that has to outlast the session.
  • The script the app writes passed scopus_cache_dir() itself to every plan, so one plan’s checkpoints overwrote another’s and each rerun paid for them again. It now keeps each plan’s checkpoints in a directory of their own under scopus_cache_dir(), named from the query and the years with a short hash added. The script opens with the scopusflow version that wrote it, notes when demo mode was on, saves the records before it plots and plots only where ggplot2 is installed. A comparison run with Partition by year off, which covers the last six years, was left out of the script and is now written over those years. The README and the articles likewise give each plan a directory of its own under scopus_cache_dir().
  • The request count of a topic comparison was understated in the help for scopus_compare_topics(), the app, the generated script and two articles. It is (terms + 1) × years, since the reference is counted in every year too, so the app’s default of two terms over six years makes 18 requests, where its note said 12. The app’s advice to use fewer terms or years now applies above 80 requests counted this way.
  • The app’s Records tab now says how many records the harvest holds and that its table shows the first 25 of them. A failed harvest is reported in the worker’s own words, where the notification opened with the “in callr subprocess” wrapper of the background process, and an error raised by scopusflow is marked “Scopus:”, as the other panels mark theirs. The year slider opens on 2015 to 2024, the span of the bundled corpus that demo mode replays, as the Python app’s slider does. The app reads that corpus as scopusflow::example_records, so demo mode works when the app is launched as scopusflow::run_app() without attaching the package, where Check size and Fetch records failed with “object ‘example_records’ not found”.
  • scopus_diff_dois() now says how many records it could not compare for want of a DOI, in the attributes n_old_without_doi and n_new_without_doi and on its printed line. Such records, 11 of the 138 in the bundled corpus, used to vanish from the diff without a count. It also orders its rows the same way on every machine, in byte order as the Python twin does, where it followed the locale’s collation and an English locale put 10.1016/j.cell before 10.1016/S0140. The tracking article advised preferring the ‘Scopus’ identifier, which no function supported, and now points to scopus_diff_records().
  • A cache_dir that cannot be written is now refused with scopus_error_bad_input before any request, in scopus_fetch_plan(), scopus_abstract() and scopus_corpus(). A checkpoint that cannot be written all the same, for example on a full disk, gives a scopus_warning_cache_unwritable warning, and its records are kept in the result. Both used to spend the cell’s quota and then lose its records to an untyped “cannot open the connection” error. The scopus_cache_clear() example no longer deletes a real managed cache when the examples are run, since it now points the cache at a temporary directory first.
  • autoplot() of a record set no longer draws zero bars for years its plan never searched. The bars ran from the first year in the records to the last, so a plan over 2015, 2016, 2019 and 2020 showed 2017 and 2018 as years without publications. They now cover the years the plan searched, each year cell or every year of a single cell’s range, and a year without records is still drawn as a zero bar. A set without a plan keeps the span of its own years. The Python twin’s year_counts() counts the same years, held to a shared fixture.
  • Trend figures now say when their last year was still being indexed. scopus_trend() records when it counted, in the retrieved_at attribute. plot_scopus_trend() and autoplot() then add a caption line such as “2026 was incomplete when retrieved on 2026-09-29.” when the years plotted reach that year. ‘Scopus’ goes on indexing a year’s publications after the year has begun, so the last point of such a figure was a count so far, easily read as a decline. The line is read from the recorded time, never from the session’s clock, so a trend tallied by hand is drawn as before. The Python twin’s plot_trend() adds the same note.
  • scopus_fetch() no longer loses records when a page comes back shorter than it asked for in the middle of a result set, as a server that caps its pages below page_size returns it. Offset paging advanced by the page size it had requested, stepping over the records between those received and the next offset, and took the short page for the last, so 20 of 60 such records came back without a warning. It now advances by the records received and stops at an empty page, and a retrieval that ends short of the total the API reported warns with scopus_warning_shortfall, as each cell of scopus_fetch_plan() already did. A retrieval stopped by max_results or at the offset ceiling is short by request and does not warn.
  • Every file the package writes is UTF-8 in every locale: a record set’s .csv, the DOI list, BibTeX, RIS, the search record and the app’s script. In a C or single-byte locale, R wrote each character the locale cannot encode as the text <U+00ED>, so a record set did not survive a .csv round trip and a reference manager was given misspelt names.
  • read_scopus_records() reads a .csv as UTF-8 whatever the locale, and reads a blank field as missing, as it reads NA. pandas, and so the Python twin, and spreadsheet software write a missing value as an empty field, which arrived as an empty string. dedupe = "id_then_doi" took such a blank identifier for an identifier and merged every unidentified record of a file the Python twin wrote into one, where that twin falls back to the DOI. The twins now keep the same rows, which a fixture both suites read pins down.
  • scopus_top(by = "author"), as_bibtex(), as_ris() and as_bibliometrix() split an author list at the semicolon with or without the space after it, as the Python twin does. Version 0.3.0 of that twin joined the authors with ";" alone, so a set it wrote counted here as one author per record.
  • plot_scopus_comparison() writes each count in its label on its own, as the Python twin writes it. format() padded the smaller counts to the width of the largest, as in a (n = 1,990).
  • The app’s Author choice under Search in sends AUTH, the tag scopus_field_tags() lists and the Python app sends under the same label. It sent AUTHLASTNAME, which searches surnames alone.
  • The app sends the query it shows. The script panel trimmed the search terms while Check size, Compare topics and Fetch records sent them as typed, so a query pasted with surrounding space went to the API inside the field tag and into the search record. All of them now trim it as the Python app does, no-break spaces included.
  • The app’s size note goes when the search it priced changes, where it went on standing for the plan on screen, and when a later check fails or a harvest starts. Check size waits while a harvest is running, since a count runs on the one Shiny thread and would freeze the live terminal, and the note writes a count such as 100,000 in full, where it read 1e+05.
  • The app’s export buttons arrive with what they write, the record exports after a harvest and the comparison’s after a comparison. Each download opens with req(), and a click with nothing to write failed in the browser with nothing on screen to say why. A demo comparison carries a note that its counts are illustrative, as the Python app’s does, since the figure’s caption names the Search API as its source.
  • The app’s panels say what they have none of. A harvest that matched nothing, or one whose source titles or author names are all missing, showed a plotting function’s error in By year, Top sources and Top authors. A highlighted topic whose counts all came back missing no longer replaces the comparison figure with an error, and is drawn without the highlight, as in the Python app. The live terminal of a demo harvest no longer labels a run over every year with the year 0, and it names a year outside the bundled corpus and the year it is drawn from.
  • The app is easier to use with a screen reader and to read. Its key status used Bootstrap’s .text-info, .text-warning and .text-success, at about 1.7:1, 1.5:1 and 4.1:1 on the sidebar’s ground, under the 4.5:1 text needs, and now uses their -emphasis variants. The progress bar carries an aria-label and, once a cell has finished, its value. Each figure carries a text alternative naming what it shows, where it was described as “Plot object”, which needs shiny 1.6.0 or later.

Documentation

  • The help for scopus_count(), scopus_fetch(), scopus_intersections() and scopus_plan() now says how years is sent. These functions, and a plan with partition = "none", send one inclusive range from the earliest year to the latest, so c(2015, 2020) covers every year from 2015 to 2020. scopus_trend(), scopus_compare_topics() and a plan with partition = "year" take each listed year.
  • citation("scopusflow"), the website and CITATION.cff give the DOI that CRAN assigned to the package, https://doi.org/10.32614/CRAN.package.scopusflow, in place of the Zenodo concept DOI. It names the R package across all its versions, and it is the DOI that the CRAN page and the citation R generates for a CRAN package already gave, so the package no longer circulates under two. Zenodo still archives every GitHub release, and CITATION.cff lists both identifiers. The CRAN DOI and the Zenodo DOI are shown as full links on the website and in the README, and the sidebar of the home page shows the CRAN DOI once: the DOI badge in the README no longer appears there a second time.
  • The README no longer names the version CRAN carries. The README inside the 0.4.0 tarball said CRAN carried 0.1.0, because the figure was typed by hand and a README is built before CRAN accepts a submission. The installation section now points to NEWS for what each release added.
  • The spelling test now fails a check run with NOT_CRAN set, as in devtools::check() and on GitHub Actions, where an unknown word used to surface only as a NOTE that left the run green. CRAN and a plain R CMD check still skip the test. The word list gains the twelve names and terms that had slipped past it.
  • ?scopus_search_report lists cells_reported, the number of plan cells that reported a total, among the elements of the record it returns.
  • The live tests run only where SCOPUSFLOW_LIVE_TESTS is "true", which the weekly live-check workflow sets. They ran wherever NOT_CRAN was "true" and a key was present, and devtools::test(), devtools::check() and testthat::test_local() set NOT_CRAN themselves, so every local run of the suite by someone keeping the key in ~/.Renviron, as ?scopus_has_key recommends, spent live quota.
  • The designing-queries article explains loose and exact phrases, and replaces its spelling-variant example, which ‘Scopus’ matches without help, with two phrases naming one condition. It also shows why a query written by hand that mixes operators needs brackets, under both the documented operator order and the one Elsevier has announced.
  • The designing-queries article describes the offline query checks and gives a recipe for testing a strategy’s relative recall against records known to be relevant, with two searches per chain of DOIs (Sampson et al., 2006; Bramer et al., 2018). The recipe contacts the API and is not run in the article.
  • The worked examples no longer present TITLE-ABS-KEY(graphene supercapacitor) as the search behind the bundled corpus. The corpus came from OpenAlex’s exact-phrase search for “graphene supercapacitor” in titles and abstracts, limited to journal articles. ‘Scopus’ joins the words of an unquoted phrase with AND, so that query is far broader, and in OpenAlex the unquoted words match about a hundred times as many records. The demonstration plan and the live searches shown beside the corpus now quote the phrase, and the help for example_records names the query the examples send. The tracking article says that a live comparison needs a baseline of your own, since the bundled one came from OpenAlex. The PRISMA-S demonstrations label their hand-set attributes, the reported totals among them, as illustrative and say that the paragraph they print describes no search that was run.
  • The keywords-and-references article no longer prints invented author keywords, four references for a paper that cites 103 works, authors in a form the parser never writes and an invented quota beneath real calls on a real DOI. The calls are shown without output, the shapes they return are built in view from example_records, and keyword stand-ins drawn from its 138 titles are counted in pairs, as in the Python guide.

scopusflow 0.4.0

CRAN release: 2026-08-21

A release about reporting a search and about trusting the cache. The package now writes a search up as the reproducible record a systematic review has to publish, and a family of silent cache defects that served the wrong records is fixed.

Writing up a search

  • scopus_search_report() assembles the reproducible search-strategy record a systematic review has to report, from a harvest or from a plan not yet run. It prints as a readable report, formats as a methods paragraph fit to paste into a manuscript (format(report, style = "paragraph")), and writes as Markdown when file is supplied. It carries the database and platform, the field-wrapped query of every cell, the year limits, view, page size and paging mode, the date searched, the records retrieved against the number the API reported as matching, per-cell completeness, duplicates removed, the software versions, a runnable snippet that rebuilds the plan, and an explicit map of which PRISMA-S items the package can supply and which only you can. The reporting standard is PRISMA-S (Rethlefsen et al., 2021, Systematic Reviews, 10, 39), with the identification counts of the PRISMA 2020 flow diagram.

    Because the output is written for a published methods section, the report states only what the objects record. An absent retrieval time is never replaced by the current one, a completeness figure is never given for a harvest whose reported total is unknown, duplicates are counted only where a merge recorded removing them, and every unverifiable field says it is unrecorded, in words. Ten of the sixteen PRISMA-S items, among them peer review of the strategy, grey literature and any other database searched, are listed as yours to supply, since the package has no evidence for them.

  • scopus_fetch_plan() now carries the per-cell accounting onto its result, as the cell_totals attribute, and sums it into total_results when (and only when) every cell reported a total. A cell that comes back shorter than the API said it should now warns, which the Python twin has done since 0.3.0, and the warning text is byte-identical between the two. A cell stopped by max_results is short by request and does not warn.

  • scopus_combine() records the merge in the combined attribute: how many records went in, how many were kept, how many were removed and whether de-duplication ran. That count exists only at the moment of the merge, and PRISMA-S asks for it.

  • A retrieval also records how it was paged, as the paging attribute, since an offset-paged query stops at the API’s ceiling where a cursor-paged one does not.

Cache defects that returned the wrong records

All were silent, and all are fixed.

  • A year-partitioned plan could be served another plan’s years, because checkpoints were keyed by the cell’s position alone and every cell of such a plan carries the same query (the year travels separately, as the API’s date parameter), so the guard meant to reject a foreign checkpoint could not tell 2015’s from 2016’s. A plan over 2016:2017 pointed at a cache written by a plan over 2015:2016 returned the 2015 records and reported “loaded from cache”. Checkpoints are now named cell-NNN-YYYY.rds and carry a manifest (query, date, view, page size and record cap) that resume compares against. Existing caches become invisible and refetch once, which spends a little quota to buy back correctness.
  • A cell cached under a max_results cap was served to a later request asking for more. The manifest now records the cap and whether it actually bit, so a truncated checkpoint is a miss for a wider request while an untruncated one stays usable for any request. The Shiny app’s cache key gained the record cap and now hashes the query, where it used to truncate it at 80 characters, so two long queries sharing a prefix no longer share a directory.
  • A zero-row checkpoint answered for any query. The guard that recognises a foreign checkpoint reads the cached rows’ query column, which an empty cell has no rows to carry, and the manifest comparison never consulted its own copy of the query, so a plan that legitimately found nothing left a checkpoint that a different plan pointed at the same cache_dir would load as its own empty result. The manifest’s query must now match as well.
  • A failed abstract retrieval was checkpointed as if it were data. A rate-limited, server-error or offline attempt in scopus_abstract() degrades to an all-NA row so the batch survives, but that row was written to the cache, so a resumed run read the failure back from disk and never retried it. Only rows parsed from successful responses are checkpointed now.
  • Two identifiers could share one abstract checkpoint, because the cache filename reduces every non-alphanumeric character to _, so distinct identifiers such as 10.1/a.b and 10.1/a-b collide on the same file, and resume never asked which identifier a cached row belonged to. The cached row’s own id must now match, and a collision warns and refetches.
  • A checkpoint holding more records than the current max_results asks for is now served trimmed to that cap, with the fuller set left on disk for a later, wider request. The opposite direction, a checkpoint truncated below what is asked for, already refetched with a warning.

A rejected or damaged checkpoint now warns, where it used to be mentioned only under verbose, and checkpoints are written to a sibling temporary file and renamed into place, so an interrupted run can no longer leave a half-written file that breaks every later resume.

Other fixes

  • scopus_combine() handed the merged set one input’s own retrieval attributes. rbind() keeps those of its first argument, so the result inherited that harvest’s plan, cell_totals and total_results even though it held the rows of several, contradicting the documented promise that per-retrieval attributes are not carried over. A search record read off the inherited total then called the union of two harvests complete against a figure belonging to one of them. Only what survives a merge is kept now: the earliest retrieval time, every contributing version, the paging mode where the inputs agree, and the merge counts themselves.
  • The PRISMA 2020 identification block counted the records identified after de-duplication, so the two figures it gives could not both be right: the diagram subtracts the duplicates removed from the records identified to reach the records screened, and 138 identified less 11 removed is not the 138 rows the set holds. Where a merge recorded how many records went into it, that is now the identification count.
  • A plan not yet run was described in the past tense, and its date line said the set did not carry a retrieval time, when the truth was that no retrieval had happened.
  • average_comparison_percentage summed the numerator over years the denominator excluded, so a year with a missing reference count inflated it, giving a figure that contradicted the per-year shares printed beside it and that drives the topic ordering in plot_scopus_comparison(). It is now computed over the years where both counts are available.
  • scopus_abstract(include = "references") aborted the whole batch when one document’s response omitted its reference-count attribute. Because that arrived as a bare base error, untyped and so outside the scopus_error hierarchy, the per-identifier handler could not catch it, defeating the documented promise that one bad identifier does not lose a batch.
  • The app’s demo banner still called the demo data synthetic, which was true of the six invented rows that shipped before 0.3.0. Demo mode has replayed 138 real published articles since then, and only the topic comparison is simulated, so the banner now says which is which.
  • A record count past 2^31 was coerced to NA at three points, each of which accepted any finite whole number and then reached for a 32-bit integer. scopus_top(n = ) left head.data.frame() raising an untyped error about its own argument; scopus_fetch(max_results = ) and scopus_fetch_plan(max_results = ) turned every later n >= max_results into NA, so the retrieval died on a bare “missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed”; and the app’s reproducible-code panel wrote max_results = NA into a script it promises is runnable. All three now carry the value as a double, so a cap wider than the result set simply never bites, which is what the Python twin has always done. A cap that fits stays an integer.
  • The 5000-record cap warning fired even when max_results had already asked for fewer records than the ceiling, advising a remedy for a problem the caller did not have.
  • scopus_compare_topics() carries its counts as doubles, matching scopus_trend() and scopus_intersections(), so billion-scale totals no longer coerce to NA.
  • Every request carries a 60-second transfer timeout, tunable through getOption("scopusflow.timeout"), so a stalled connection cannot hang a session.
  • Retrievals record when they were taken and by which package version, as the retrieved_at and scopusflow_version attributes, preserved through the .rds round trip. Both are attributes, so the documented schema and the CSV round trip are unchanged.
  • Every text file the package writes now carries LF line endings on all platforms: the BibTeX and RIS exports, the DOI and record CSVs, and the app’s script and comparison downloads previously arrived with CRLF endings when written on Windows.
  • Every print() method now sends its whole output to standard output. The header line went through cli, which writes to the message stream, so capture.output() returned the table without its header, and a knitted document showed one printed object as two separate blocks.

Continuous integration and metadata

  • The dependency canary could finish green having exercised nothing, when no development head was actually installed. It now says so, in a warning and in the step summary, and it installs the ggplot2 development head alongside the Imports.
  • The declared dependency floors are now installed and tested by a min-deps job, and the check matrix reaches back to roughly R 4.3.
  • rlang’s floor is corrected to 1.1.0. The evidence for it is httr2 1.0.0’s own DESCRIPTION, which requires rlang (>= 1.1.0), so the old floor described a combination no user could have installed. It is CRAN-visible metadata.
  • The documented request cost of the live API check, the cache guard’s description in the documentation and vignette, and the path to the Python twin’s copy of the example records were all corrected.

scopusflow 0.3.0

A data and documentation release. The bundled corpus becomes a real harvest, and every example and article is rebuilt on it.

The bundled example records

The dataset the package ships for offline work was replaced outright.

  • example_records is now a worked example harvest of 138 real journal articles on graphene supercapacitors published between 2015 and 2024, carrying their real titles, DOIs, source titles, first authors and citation counts. It replaces the six invented records shipped previously.
  • The records are not a ‘Scopus’ harvest and are not described as one. The Elsevier API terms do not permit redistributing retrieved records, so they come from OpenAlex, whose metadata is released under CC0, reshaped into the schema [scopus_fetch()] returns. The reasoning is recorded in the design notes.
  • The harvest is complete, so the rows per year are the real publications per year for that query. Eleven records carry no DOI and two no source title, kept as they arrive because a real harvest has such gaps.
  • scopus_id is empty throughout, these records not having come from ‘Scopus’, so de-duplication falls back to the DOI as it does for any record whose identifier is missing.

Documentation

The material a reader meets was rebuilt on the new corpus, and one misleading fixture was replaced.

  • Every vignette and example runs on that corpus, paired with the key-gated live call a reader would write, and the figures quoted in the prose were recomputed against the new data.
  • The demo mode of run_app() draws on the same corpus, so a first look at the app opens on real articles, where it used to show invented rows.
  • The parser fixture in inst/extdata moves onto the reserved 10.5555 example prefix. It previously paired genuine, resolving DOIs with invented titles and authors, so a reader who checked one found a real paper mislabelled.
  • Every vignette now turns console colour off and fixes the console width while it renders. pkgdown enables colour for its own build, and the escape sequences were reaching the reader as literal text in the middle of the tables.
  • vignette("comparing-topics") shows one year of its illustrative comparison across every topic, in place of the whole table, and leaves out the query column, which in a real comparison holds the whole query string and so reads badly in a table.
  • The README no longer opens with a link to the documentation site, which on the site’s own home page pointed the reader at the page in front of them.

scopusflow 0.2.1

A documentation release. The vignettes now demonstrate several features that 0.2.0 shipped but did not show.

  • vignette("designing-queries") shows the AND NOT operator in [scopus_query()], excluding a dominant homonym from a search.
  • vignette("analysing-a-literature") passes [scopus_intersections()] a concept that is already a complete field-tagged expression and so is used as given, letting a concept be a whole synonym set.
  • vignette("scopusflow") introduces [scopus_top()] on a record set, and points to the analysis article for the plots and trends built on it.
  • vignette("plans-and-quota") covers verbose = TRUE in [scopus_fetch_plan()], which reports a line as each cell is fetched or loaded from cache.
  • vignette("building-a-reference-set") shows [scopus_extract_dois()] on a plain vector of DOIs, both with the default deduplication (which ignores case and resolver prefixes) and with dedupe = FALSE.
  • vignette("keywords-and-references") tallies author keywords across a [scopus_corpus()] result, the per-keyword document count the article is named for.
  • [scopus_abstract()]’s help page no longer describes the Python twin’s reference fields.

scopusflow 0.2.0

This release reaches further into the API, adds an analysis and export layer on top of a retrieval, and introduces a local, code-free app.

Deeper retrieval

A search now reaches further into the API, past the offset ceiling and beyond the fields the Search endpoint returns.

  • [scopus_fetch()] gains cursor = TRUE, cursor-based pagination that retrieves a whole large query without the 5000-record ceiling of offset paging. The warning on a query that exceeds the ceiling suggests this alongside partitioning with [scopus_plan()].
  • [scopus_fetch()] and [scopus_fetch_plan()] add an authkeywords column when view = "COMPLETE" is requested, at no cost beyond that view’s own smaller page size. The view = "STANDARD" output is unchanged, and [read_scopus_records()] keeps the column across a CSV round-trip.
  • [scopus_abstract()] retrieves the abstract and fuller metadata for one or many records from the ‘Scopus’ Abstract Retrieval API, resilient to an identifier that cannot be found. Through view and include = c("references", "keywords") it also retrieves a document’s own reference list, as a structured, per-citation data frame, and author keywords, with per-identifier caching keyed by the requested view and extras, an n_requests/quota attribute, and a clear, actionable error on an entitlement 403 that stops the batch, so the same failure is not repeated for every identifier. include = "keywords" without view = "FULL" is rejected up front, since the REF response carries no author keywords.
  • [scopus_corpus()] combines a search result with abstract retrieval into a minimal id/title/year/keywords/references shape for downstream tools such as keyword co-occurrence or citation-network analysis, without replacing [as_bibliometrix()]. A new vignette, Author keywords and references, walks through all of this with real DOIs.
  • [scopus_fetch_plan()] compares each checkpoint’s recorded query with the plan cell before loading it, refetching and overwriting the checkpoint on a mismatch, so two different plans pointed at the same cache_dir cannot serve each other’s records. A checkpoint that carries no query information (a zero-row cell, or one written by scopusflow 0.1.0) loads as before, and a cache directory is still best kept to a single plan.

Analysis and plots

The package gains a layer for summarising a literature and drawing the result.

  • [scopus_trend()] reports annual record counts for a query (the size of a literature over time), with [plot_scopus_trend()].
  • [scopus_top()] tallies the most frequent sources or authors in a record set, with [plot_scopus_top()], which draws whole-number axis breaks (so a tally of small counts shows no fractional ticks) and derives the count axis’s headroom from the widest end-of-bar label (so a wide count, say five figures on a top-authors bar, does not clip at the panel edge). An autoplot() method draws a record set’s publications per year.
  • [scopus_intersections()] counts a named set of concepts and any requested intersections of them, sizing where a study or a niche sits within the surrounding literature at one count request per row. Concept values that are already complete field-tagged expressions are used exactly as given, with no second wrap. [plot_scopus_intersections()] draws the result as a lollipop chart on a log-scale axis, with an autoplot() method and an optional highlight (for example the niche itself) whose legend label is derived from what is highlighted: ‘Focal intersection’ for intersections, ‘Focal concept’ for concepts and ‘Focal set’ for a mixture. An explicit highlight_label still wins.
  • [plot_scopus_comparison()] gains legend_inside. When set, and a legend is drawn, it is placed inside the panel in whichever corner has the most free space, on a small semi-transparent background, where the default places it above the panel. That default is unchanged.
  • [plot_scopus_comparison()] now spreads the direct line labels vertically so topics that converge near the final year no longer overlap, and falls back to a legend when there are too many topics to label legibly. The labels are spread when the figure is drawn, against the rendered text height, so they stay legible at any figure size, including a short panel such as the app’s result card. They carry no leader lines. The labels are colour-matched to their lines and spread in the same order as the line ends, so the link is clear without a leader that would otherwise cut across neighbouring labels.

Export

A retrieval can now leave the package in the formats other tools read.

  • [as_bibtex()] and [as_ris()] export a record set to the BibTeX and RIS interchange formats, so a search can be carried into Zotero, EndNote, Mendeley or a LaTeX bibliography.

A code-free app

The whole workflow is now available without writing any R.

  • [run_app()] launches a local, code-free Shiny app for building a search, retrieving records with a live progress terminal, and exporting them. A panel mirrors every choice as a runnable R script, so the app is an on-ramp to the package. It runs on your own machine, so the API key never leaves it. The app also has a Compare topics tab (with highlight, stability-band and counts-in-label controls, a per-term progress indicator, a quota estimate and a CSV export) and a Demo mode, on by default, that synthesises records and a comparison so the whole workflow can be explored with no key and no network. A new vignette, Using the code-free app, walks through every panel.
  • The app holds steady under stress. It refuses to start a comparison while a harvest is running, turns any comparison failure into a notification, floors a fractional maximum-records entry, drops duplicate comparison terms, and tells you when there is nothing to cancel.

Other improvements

One rough edge in the package’s messaging was smoothed.

  • The no-key error renders its guidance (the option name, the api_key argument and the key-request URL) through cli, where it used to leak raw markup.

scopusflow 0.1.0

CRAN release: 2026-06-20

First release.

  • Reproducible search plans with [scopus_plan()], and cheap sizing with [scopus_count()].
  • Quota-aware, paginated retrieval through [scopus_fetch()], with the largest page each view allows requested by default to keep request counts low, and resumable, cached, partitioned retrieval through [scopus_fetch_plan()].
  • A stable normalised record schema from [scopus_records()], with a summary() method that gives a quick overview.
  • DOI extraction and change tracking with [scopus_extract_dois()] and [scopus_diff_dois()].
  • Topic-trend comparison with [scopus_compare_topics()], and a plot from [plot_scopus_comparison()] or autoplot().
  • Interoperability and I/O through [as_bibliometrix()], [write_scopus_records()] and [read_scopus_records()].
  • A reference to the common ‘Scopus’ field tags in [scopus_field_tags()], a safe query composer in [scopus_query()], and a bundled [example_records] dataset for offline exploration.
  • Safe merging of record sets with [scopus_combine()] (and a c() method), plus as_tibble() and as.data.frame() coercion.
  • A typed condition system (scopus_error and its subclasses) and quota-header parsing with [scopus_quota()].
  • The comparison plot uses whole-number year breaks, a colour-blind-safe palette, direct line labels, an optional highlight argument and a shaded Wilson stability band (an illustrative range, switchable with interval).
  • The bundled example_records spans several disciplines, and the examples and five workflow vignettes draw on a wide range of fields.
  • The authors column retains every author a record lists. Very large result totals are handled without overflow, and DOI cleaning copes with www.doi.org hosts and DOI: labels.
